lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Greenleaf Florist | Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Delivered 30 to 40 arrangements a day across the city and took cash and card payments at the door.
- Prepared weekend wedding orders with the head florist and kept the cooler stocked and labeled.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Owned the pick-path layouts for the fast-moving zone and the labor reports the shift leads used.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; the findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.

- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations while also covering night-shift supervision, updating the safety training slides, coordinating holiday temp hiring and running the forklift certification schedule, which raised inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5%.
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Reduced freight costs by 15% by consolidating supplier pickups into regional milk runs.
- Set reorder points for every SKU from 18 months of daily demand and supplier lead-time data, reviewed monthly with the category managers.
- Built the weekly supplier scorecard for 40 vendors, which buyers used to renegotiate delivery windows with the five least reliable.
- Raised the packaging line's overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 71% to 112% by cutting changeover time and micro-stops.
- Cut average order lead time through the warehouse from 10 days to 5 while holding daily throughput constant and doubling work-in-process to keep pickers busy.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Checked the planned routes against 4 weeks of real delivery logs; planned drive times came within 5% of the actual ones.
- Shared the model and a one-page summary with the grocer's dispatch team, who piloted the routes on two trucks for a month.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- The donation intake process was mapped and two duplicate data-entry steps were removed, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Built a seasonal forecast for 1,400 products across three warehouses that more than halved stockouts and cut inventory by nearly $2M.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: Experience is not in reverse chronological order because Lakeview appears before the more recent Crestway role.
items.because: The order can make readers misread the career timeline and delays the more relevant planner experience.

items.says: The 2018 degree appears before the more relevant professional experience.
items.because: Leading with education makes the résumé read like an early-career document.

items.says: The current Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant title creates an unexplained seniority reversal after the Supply Chain Planner role.
items.because: Without context, recruiters may question the candidate’s direction and overlook the relevant experience.

items.says: The Greenleaf entry occupies too much space for a job that does not support the operations and supply-chain direction.
items.because: Two duty bullets compete with more relevant analytical work and reinforce the apparent seniority reversal.

items.says: “Delivered” and “took” use past tense for a current role.
The delivery volume does not show a service outcome.
“Prepared” and “kept” use past tense for a current role.
“Prepared weekend wedding orders” does not identify the actual preparation work.
The cooler-stocked-and-labeled duty does not say what it enabled or prevented.
“Owned the pick-path layouts” frames an assignment rather than an analytical action.
items.because: “Owned” establishes responsibility without showing what the candidate did to the layouts.

items.says: The pick-path and labor-report work has no stated operational result.
items.because: A hiring manager cannot tell whether either workstream improved an operating measure.

items.says: The named deliverables do not show the analysis used to develop them.
“The findings led to a triage station” hides the candidate’s role in the change.
items.because: It is unclear whether the candidate recommended or implemented the station, or only reported the study.

items.says: “Dock scheduling rules” does not show the scheduling approach.
items.because: A defining rule or constraint would make the trailer-wait improvement technically credible.

items.says: The strongest Lakeview achievement appears after a weaker opening bullet.
items.because: Putting the 95-to-40-minute improvement first would establish the entry’s scale and impact.

items.says: Four unrelated duties interrupt the cycle-counting achievement.
items.because: They turn a strong inventory-control result into a task list and make it harder to scan.

items.says: The inventory-accuracy gain is ambiguously attached to five activities rather than cycle counting.
items.because: A reader may credit the gain to the combined duty list instead of the cycle-counting program.

items.says: The 15% freight-cost reduction lacks a cost basis and comparison period.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what cost measure was reduced or how the reduction was calculated.

items.says: The reorder-point work gives no resulting change in replenishment performance.
items.because: Without a downstream result, the effectiveness of the planning work remains unproven.

items.says: The line names data inputs without explaining the reorder-point logic.
items.because: The inputs alone do not show how the candidate set the thresholds.

items.says: “Reviewed monthly with the category managers” could modify either the data or the reorder points.
items.because: The construction leaves what was reviewed unclear and understates the candidate’s role.

items.says: The scorecard line does not say whether supplier performance improved after buyers renegotiated delivery windows.
items.because: Adoption by buyers does not show what the renegotiations accomplished.

items.says: “Supplier scorecard” does not identify the measures used to evaluate vendors.
“The five least reliable” is inconsistent with the entry’s use of numerals for quantities.
An OEE increase from 71% to 112% is impossible under the conventional definition.
items.because: OEE’s components are each capped at 100%, so OEE cannot exceed 100%.

items.says: The line names losses that declined rather than the actions that reduced them.
items.because: A manufacturing reader cannot see what intervention produced the improvement.

items.says: Halving lead time at constant throughput is inconsistent with doubling work-in-process.
items.because: Under Little’s Law, work-in-process would halve if throughput stayed constant and lead time fell from 10 days to 5.

items.says: The lead-time reduction does not identify the operational change that produced it.
items.because: The reader cannot identify the candidate’s contribution or distinguish it from a broader operating change.

items.says: Doubling work-in-process to keep pickers busy reads as queueing rather than a business benefit.
items.because: The tradeoff dominates the achievement and leaves its customer-service value unclear.

items.says: “As a vehicle-routing problem” does not explain how the routes were optimized.
The planned-mileage comparison is awkward and repeats “routes.”
The 5% drive-time difference does not specify how it was aggregated.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it is a mean, median, total, or per-route difference.

items.says: “Real” is a filler word in “real delivery logs.”
The pilot gives no observed operating outcome.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it reduced mileage, saved time, improved completion, or informed a decision.

items.says: Sharing the model and summary is foregrounded instead of the stronger pilot.
items.because: The month-long operational pilot is more persuasive than delivering materials.

items.says: “Two trucks” is inconsistent with the entry’s use of numerals for quantities.
“Analyzed warehouse operations” does not identify what was examined or how.
The recommendations statement ends with advice rather than its adoption or effect.
The generic opening does not organize the donation-intake and forecasting workstreams.
items.because: It gives no shared objective or method, so the work reads as disconnected projects.

items.says: The donation-intake changes are described in passive voice.
items.because: The construction hides the candidate and team as the actors behind the one-day improvement.

items.says: The forecast achievement is duplicated from Crestway and attributed to the food-bank project.
items.because: The matching scope and outcomes create a serious credibility problem for both entries.

items.says: The seasonal forecast does not identify its method or principal inputs.
items.because: The reader cannot assess the analytical work behind the claim.

items.says: The stockout reduction lacks a baseline and comparison period.
items.because: The reader cannot determine the starting level or when the improvement was measured.

items.says: The nearly $2M inventory reduction does not identify the financial measure.
items.because: It could mean inventory value, purchases, carrying cost, or another measure.

items.says: The claimed results are buried, and the bullet is not first in the entry.
items.because: If verified as food-bank work, those results would be the entry’s strongest evidence.
